related_resources.reason: Sixth–seventh-century sealing with five impressions; more than 500 sealings excavated at a burned fortress near Shiraz. This is an object record, not a full administrative archive.
Explains how clay sealings were attached, the distinctions between personal and office seals, and archives preserved by fires; some functions remain contested.
Overview of civil and military ranks, fiscal jurisdictions and the use of official clay sealings; abstract alone cannot support granular reconstructions.
Reports 559 clay bullae, with 22 administrative sealings; institutional attributions and provincial links are specialist interpretations of seal inscriptions. Full article not examined.
Examines 73 returned bullae and nearly 244 impressions; likely connected to an antiquities collection but archaeological provenance is not secured.
Discusses judges, appeals, priestly authority, social status, marriage categories and limitations of surviving legal texts; norms cannot be taken as comprehensive lived practice.
